summary: Former Hastings County township, now part of Tweed. The index's coordinates lie far northwest of it, and no source describes the tower.

corrections.proposed: Unconfirmed. The name matches former Grimsthorpe Township, Hastings County (now Tweed); no source confirms the tower's site.
corrections.why: The index coordinates are far northwest of Tweed, which contains former Grimsthorpe Township. Tweed's article and the Heritage PIN both place the township in Hastings County.

notes_for_editor: The index's coordinates (45.71394, -82.32414) are far northwest of Tweed, the municipality that absorbed Grimsthorpe Township, so they probably belong to another place or are mistyped. I found no source giving a replacement position, so the location correction stays open. No readable source gives the tower's build year, design, height, staffing, fate or current access; the index shows N/A for design, height, elevation and year built. The Tweed Forest Fire District (1922) is context only, and no source ties this tower to it. The Heritage PIN page cites a 1927 history for the 1822 detail (Jesse E. Middleton, The Province of Ontario: a History: 1615-1927); I did not read that book.
